transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-01 10:00 PDT
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Jordan Brooks (Redwood); Priya Singh, Tom Keller, Sara Lopez (Ravenfall)

Summary:
Quick kickoff to align on onboarding runway for Ravenfall's summary-generation inference use case. Primary asks: VPC/on-prem options, SSO + RBAC, KMS integration, latency SLOs for 95th pct, and a short pilot (2-3 weeks) to validate cost/latency.

Topics covered:
- Current infra & constraints
- Security and compliance requirements (SOC2, KMS, SAML)
- Runtime choices: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
- Benchmark and pilot plan
- Next steps and owners

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, looks like we've got a full house, um quick intros — i'm Maya from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account. jordan, meet the ravenfall crew?
[00:12] Jordan: hey all, jordan brooks, SE, i'll be driving the runtime and the bench stuff.
[00:18] Priya: priya singh, head of ml at ravenfall. we'll be leading the integration on our side.
[00:22] Tom: tom keller, vp engineering, i'll be partnering on infra and security sign-off.
[00:26] Sara: sara lopez, secops, i'll be the compliance / networking contact.
[00:34] Maya: awesome. goal for today is to map out the onboarding runway — get clarity on VPC vs dedicated, what security artifacts you need, and agree on pilot scope. if we can get those things we can kick off a pilot mid-aug. sound good?
[00:45] Priya: yea that'd be great. we primarily want low latency for our user-facing summarization - target like 150-200ms p95 on short prompts, and cost needs to be controlled. also need strong controls on data residency and audit logs.
[00:58] Jordan: got it. just to set expec — p95 150-200ms is doable for some model sizes but depends on sequence length and the model variant; there are tradeoffs. we can talk about quantization and batching configs to bring down cost at acceptable latency.
[01:16] Tom: can you explain the difference quickly between hosted and dedicated — from an ops perspective?
[01:22] Maya: yeah hosted is our standard api — fastest to get started, runs in our cloud, includes our model catalog. dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools that you can pin to, predictable throughput and isolation. private / vpc is the third option where control plane is customer-managed and we ship a private connector, useful when you need strict network controls or air-gapped.
[01:40] Sara: for us, VPC peering or Private is preferable. our security policy requires all egress to be controlled and keys in our KMS. we also need SAML SSO and RBAC integration with our IDP.
[01:52] Jordan: that's fine — we support SAML SSO, RBAC, and KMS integrations. for keys you can bring your own KMS/HSM for private deployments; for hosted we support KMS integration too but there are different patterns.
[02:07] Priya: do you have SOC2 and pen-test reports we can share with legal?
[02:12] Maya: yes i'll share the security pack after the call; it includes SOC2 report, standard pen test summary, and a network diagram.
[02:19] Tom: good. on the runtime side, priya's team runs both short and long prompts - average token length is 60 but we have 5-10% longer tails. we need prefix caching for chat-like flows.
[02:32] Jordan: prefix caching / kv cache is supported, although the transcription sometimes says "KV cash" so apologies for autocorrects in prior docs, it's KV cache. we can configure automatic prefix cache for repeated contexts; that'll reduce token cost and improve latency.
[02:45] Priya: nice, and model pinning? we need to freeze a version during pilot.
[02:49] Maya: you can pin the model version per-route; we also support canary rollouts and automatic fallback to a cheaper variant if capacity spikes.
[02:58] Sara: fallback concerns me — if it switches to a cheaper model, do we get alerted and is there automatic QA gating?
[03:04] Jordan: yes you can set rollout policies — alerting and quality guards. re: quality, we recommend running evals on a held-out prompt set; our optimize toolkit will flag regressions.
[03:16] [03:30] Speaker 2: uh sorry small crosstalk —
[03:34] Maya: no worries. so here's a proposed pilot: 2 weeks, run on Redwood Dedicated reserved capacity with canary to hosted as fallback, measure p95, cost per 1k requests, and quality metrics on the prompt set priya provides.
[03:51] Priya: do we have example metrics you can share in the pilot template?
[03:54] Jordan: yes i'll send a template — it includes latency percentiles, token cost, model accuracy proxies, and a regression alerting threshold. we'll also include a bench harness you can run with your sample traces.
[04:08] Tom: on networking — what's required for VPC? is it straight peering or do you use a connector?
[04:14] Maya: we have two patterns: 1) VPC peering / private link into our Dedicated infra, or 2) customer-managed private deployment where the control plane is separate and inference happens in your VPC. for strict compliance you might want the second.
[04:29] Sara: the second one looks better. any extra costs / timeline implication?
[04:33] Jordan: private deployments need additional ops setup; timeline is usually 2-4 weeks for initial provisioning and validation depending on infra. Dedicated can be faster, 1–2 weeks.
[04:44] Priya: timeline's important cause we're aiming to launch an internal beta late sept. we need pilot complete by end of august.
[04:51] Maya: that timeline works if we start pilot mid-august. action items will be to exchange artifacts this week and schedule the SE deep dive next week.
[05:01] Tom: about data retention — do you persist logs indefinitely? we need audit logging but retention policies controlled by us.
[05:09] Maya: logs can be configured; for private deployments you control retention. for hosted we can provide export hooks and configurable retention windows per-tenant. we'll include the audit log sample in the pack.
[05:20] Sara: KMS — we want to BYOK and HSM-backed keys. is that supported in hosted?
[05:26] Jordan: hosted supports KMS integration but BYOK/HSM for encrypted model stores is easier on private. we'll include patterns in the security doc — there's an option with envelope encryption that meets most compliance needs.
[05:38] Priya: ok great. on models: we plan to use a mid-sized open model for quality/cost balance — we'll need guidance on quantization profiles and recommended batch sizes.
[05:50] Jordan: we'll recommend quantization and batching based on your sample trace distribution; that's part of the bench plan. a note: batching reduces cost but increases tail latency; we can profile with the harness to find operating sweet spot.
[06:03] Maya: i'll summarize the sweet spot tradeoffs in the follow-up and we'll mark which configs are recommended for the pilot.
[06:10] [06:30] Tom: any license or data usage concerns — we want to ensure our customer data isn't used to fine-tune shared models.
[06:37] Maya: by default we isolate your workloads; we also offer contractual protections and model-level isolation; we'll include language for data usage and model training in the legal pack.
[06:47] Priya: sounds good. one more — observability: can we get per-route token + latency breakdown in the console?
[06:53] Jordan: yes the Console provides per-route model, token, latency, and error traces; you can set retention windows and integrate with your datadog / sumo / splunk via export.
[07:04] Sara: perf question — do you support FPGA or only GPU backends?
[07:08] Jordan: current infra is GPU-optimized inference engine; we pick kernels per hardware. we don't support FPGA in prod at the moment.
[07:16] Priya: any other gotchas we should be aware of during pilot?
[07:20] Jordan: watch sequence-length distribution — long tails can blow up cost. also prefix cache warm-up can skew early metrics; we recommend a 24-48h soak period to stabilize caching benefits before finalizing numbers.
[07:33] Maya: ok quick recap then next steps — we'll share security docs, jordan will send piloting template and bench harness, priya will provide sample traces and SLO targets, sara will confirm VPC/contact. propose pilot kickoff 2025-08-18 pending confirmations.
[07:50] Tom: fine by me. we should also set a 30-minute demo for the eng team to review the console.
[07:57] Maya: yes i'll set a console walkthrough for devs — maybe 60 minutes.
[08:03] Priya: one ask, can you provide ephemeral test credentials for staging?
[08:07] Jordan: yes i'll provision short-lived api keys for the bench run and include instructions in the template.
[08:12] Sara: legal will want the service-levels and incident contact; ensure escalation matrix is in the pack.
[08:18] Maya: will do.
[08:22] [08:40] Speaker 1: small lag, sorry —
[08:44] Maya: no problem. any blockers on timeline from ravenfall side?
[08:48] Priya: just getting the sample traces and internal approvals — i'll prioritize and try to get them by tuesday 2025-08-05.
[08:56] Tom: we'll review the security docs with legal and get back.
[09:00] Maya: perfect. last thing — competitors question: you mentioned anthro/other vendors — any specific concerns?
[09:06] Tom: just comparing cost and SLA commitments. also want to know how we can minimize vendor lock-in.
[09:12] Jordan: we recommend clear model pinning and exportable configs; we also provide artifact export and runbooks so customers can re-run workloads elsewhere if needed.
[09:22] Maya: ok that's it from us — thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the pack and calendar invites.
[09:28] Priya: thanks, excited to kick this off.
[09:30] Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: occasional mislabels (Speaker 1/2) and minor word swaps e.g., 'KV cash' instead of 'KV cache' — cleaned minimally.
